increment: Two independent test-quality fixes: (1) re-point _applied_revisions() in test_category_seed_migration.py at the database (alembic_version head + ancestors) so the '>= {SEED_REVISION}' assertion is real, not vacuous; (2) widen the module-only capture.json freshness guard in test_capture_sidecar.py to a tree-wide AST guard.
part1: OLD _applied_revisions() read migration scripts on disk via walk_revisions(), so 'assert _applied_revisions() >= {SEED_REVISION}' was vacuously true (the file is in the repo, therefore the revision is in the set, regardless of any DB). Re-pointed it at the database: heads from alembic_version + ancestors via ScriptDirectory.iterate_revisions(heads,'base'). Chose re-point over rename because it makes the assertion real. A bare alembic_version read is insufficient here because 0011 stacks on top of 0010, so the seed is not the head; walking head->base recovers the full applied set. Kept the @skip_without_db gating (helper now takes engine).
part2: OLD test_no_freshness_assertion_exists_in_this_module parsed only Path(__file__), catching a clock read in test_capture_sidecar.py alone. Replaced with a tree-wide, AST-based guard: derive all test modules from TESTS_ROOT.rglob('*.py'); a module is in scope iff it uses a string constant whose Path.name == 'capture.json' (loads a committed sidecar); a scoped module must contain no wall-clock read (ast.Call attribute in {now,today,utcnow,time,monotonic}). Precise line: 'capture.json' literal, NOT the pervasive 'fetched_at' column, so legit runtime-freshness tests (assess_staleness, test_evidence_currency, test_adviser_stale_evidence) stay out of scope. Non-vacuity: >=60 test modules AND this module in the sidecar-reader set AND >=5 sidecar readers.
constraints: Do not weaken surrounding coverage; the exactly-14-canonical-slugs assertion is untouched.
Guard is AST-based, tree-derived, non-substring; prose 'freshness' must not trip it.
No fixture re-capture, no network, no npm; boundary files untouched.
acceptance: Part 1: old assertion True against a DB at 0009 (seed never applied); new assertion False there, True at 0011.

Part 2: planted freshness bomb in a file OTHER than test_capture_sidecar.py -> new guard FAILS naming file+line; old guard misses it; runtime-freshness tests still pass; count assertion fires when glob matches nothing.
Full suite + ruff check + ruff format --check green with collected counts reported.
